title: On What Basis the Unearned Part of an Auto Loans Waiver Charge Is Measured
content:
The basis on which the unearned part of the waiver charge financed with a loan of the Auto Loans line is measured follows how long the borrower's Personal Checking account has been open, counted in whole months to the day of the cancellation.

**Opened at least 120 whole months before the cancellation:** the unearned part is measured on the days remaining to the scheduled maturity over the days of the whole term.

**Opened at least 48 but less than 120 whole months before the cancellation:** the months remaining are taken up to the whole quarter above before the share is worked out.

**Opened less than 48 whole months before the cancellation:** the unearned part is measured on the whole months remaining over the term.

## What taking the months up to the whole quarter above means

The months remaining are raised to the next whole multiple of three months. A figure of 42 months is already a whole multiple of three and stays at 42. A figure of 43 months becomes 45. A figure of 41 months becomes 42. The share is then worked out on the raised figure over the term.

## The three bases on one loan

Take a loan written for 60 months whose refundable share of the charge financed at funding is 625.50, with 43 whole months remaining, 1305 days remaining to the scheduled maturity and 1826 days in the whole term. Under the first basis the unearned part is 625.50 multiplied by 1305 and divided by 1826. Under the second it is 625.50 multiplied by 45 and divided by 60. Under the third it is 625.50 multiplied by 43 and divided by 60.

## The months at which the basis changes

An account opened exactly 120 whole months before the cancellation is measured on days over days. An account opened exactly 48 whole months before has its months remaining taken up to the whole quarter above. An account opened 47 whole months before is measured on whole months over the term.
